title: Trajectory-Guided Fault Localization for Agent Skill Evolution

paragraphs.en: Agent skills provide reusable guidance for code agents, but incomplete or unsuitable guidance can impair task execution. To reduce the manual effort of skill refinement, recent approaches use LLMs to generate revisions from execution feedback. However, grounding these revisions in explicit behavioral evidence remains challenging. To address this gap, we propose SkillMorph , a skill-evolution approach based on trajectory-guided fault localization in agent skills. Its core idea is to link execution evidence to specific skill contents before generating revisions. Specifically, SkillMorph compares failure and success evidence in abstracted trajectories across repeated runs and tasks, incorporating changes between evolution loops to identify suspicious actions. It then uses these suspicious actions to localize edit sites in the skills and generate corresponding revisions. Experiments on SWE-Skills-Bench and CannBot show that the skills evolved by SkillMorph consistently achieve higher trial-level accuracy and execution consistency than the original skills and those from four existing skill-evolution methods. We have also applied SkillMorph to automated kernel generation with an AI operator-development team, which has accepted 6 skill-revision pull requests.

paragraphs.en: Agent Skills have become a common paradigm for supporting large language model (LLM)-based agents in domain-specific tasks such as software engineering [ 12 ] , data analysis [ 15 ] , and document processing [ 47 ] . Specifically, a skill packages reusable instructions, scripts, and reference materials for a specialized workflow. When carrying out a task, the agent loads the relevant skills and takes actions under their guidance, leveraging the experience encoded in those skills to solve the task more effectively. In practice, however, incomplete guidance or unsuitable workflows can lead the agent to take unsuitable actions, which limits skill effectiveness or even impairs task execution [ 10 , 12 ] . Addressing these deficiencies generally relies on domain experts to inspect the agent’s actions, trace the problematic ones back to the skill content that guided them, and iteratively revise and evaluate the guidance [ 1 , 47 ] . This manual process makes skill refinement costly and time-consuming, and difficult to scale as task and skill collections grow.

paragraphs.en: To reduce manual effort, several approaches have recently been proposed for skill evolution , which aims to improve agent performance by automatically refining skills based on execution feedback [ 44 , 46 , 1 , 33 , 23 , 31 , 48 ] . Most of these techniques follow an iterative process with two steps: (1) executing a set of evolution tasks using the current skill set to collect execution feedback, and (2) prompting an LLM with this feedback to produce a revision of the skill content. Despite the effectiveness of existing skill-evolution approaches, three challenges remain.

paragraphs.en: First , it is challenging to ground skill revision in explicit behavioral evidence. Existing approaches generally prompt an LLM to generate revisions directly from execution feedback, such as task outcomes, case-level scores, or whole trajectories [ 44 , 17 , 1 , 10 , 49 ] . Consequently, which behaviors are problematic is implicitly determined by the LLM as it reads the feedback and writes the revision, leaving no record for later inspection or comparison. This results in two consequences. On the one hand, without an explicit link between problematic behaviors and the skill content that needs correction, the revisions are likely to alter content that merely appears relevant to the observed problem while leaving the content requiring correction unchanged. Recently, ContractSkill [ 24 ] achieved explicit localization by representing a skill as an ordered sequence of steps with postconditions and using a deterministic verifier to identify the failing step. However, it assumes that the skill can be expressed in such a structured form and that a suitable verifier is available, which limits its general applicability. On the other hand, without explicit behavioral evidence, earlier revisions are difficult to reassess when a problem recurs. Several recent approaches retain historical records across evolution loops, but these records capture only scores or task-level status rather than linking targeted behaviors to edited regions [ 44 , 17 ] . Such coarse records are insufficient to distinguish an incorrect edit location from an insufficient correction at the right location. As a result, later loops may repeatedly modify the same content without resolving the deficiency, or fail to notice a regression introduced by an earlier revision.

paragraphs.en: Our Work. In this work, we propose to evolve skills via trajectory-guided fault localization , which identifies the skill contents that require revision. The key idea is that before generating any revision, we explicitly determine the edit-sites, i.e., the skill contents that should be revised, and ground this decision in behavioral evidence from execution trajectories. This idea draws on program repair, where evidence from passing and failing tests guides the localization of suspicious code before candidate patches are generated [ 38 , 36 ] . Analogously, we treat each agent execution on a task as a test execution and the actions in its trajectory as the entities covered by that execution. We localize through actions rather than treating skill contents directly as covered entities, because natural-language guidance lacks the explicit execution semantics of code. Specifically, an agent loads a skill document as a whole, and whether and how it follows each instruction is left to its own interpretation, thus there is no observable notion of which contents an execution exercises. In contrast, actions are directly observable in trajectories, differ across executions, and are shaped by the skill content. Therefore, a deficiency in a skill manifests as suspicious actions, and the trajectory records the guidance the agent consulted when taking them, allowing these actions to be traced back to the responsible skill content. By recording these actions, the edit sites derived from them, and the evidence behind both, the localization decisions become inspectable and can be reassessed when later executions reveal a persistent problem. An action also provides a common anchor for locating regions across multiple skills that jointly guide it, thus enabling coordinated revisions to those contents.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的工作。 在这项工作中，我们提出通过轨迹引导的故障定位来演化技能，该方法能够识别需要修订的技能内容。 核心思想是：在生成任何修订之前，我们会明确确定编辑位置，即应当被修订的技能内容，并将这一决策基于执行轨迹中的行为证据。 这一思路借鉴了程序修复方法，其中通过通过和失败的测试提供的证据，在生成候选补丁之前定位可疑代码 [38, 36]。 类似地，我们将智能体在任务上的每次执行视为一次测试执行，并将其轨迹中的动作视为该执行所覆盖的实体。 我们选择通过动作进行定位，而不是直接将技能内容视为被覆盖的实体，因为自然语言指导缺乏代码所具备的明确执行语义。 具体来说，智能体会将技能文档作为一个整体加载，而它是否以及如何遵循每条指令则取决于自身的解释，因此无法观察到执行究竟使用了哪些内容。 相比之下，动作在轨迹中可以直接观察，不同执行之间存在差异，并且受到技能内容的影响。 因此，技能的缺陷会表现为可疑的动作，而轨迹记录了智能体在执行这些动作时所参考的指导信息，从而可以将这些动作追溯到相应的技能内容。 通过记录这些动作、由此推导出的编辑位置以及相关的证据，定位决策就变得可审查；当后续执行暴露出持续性问题时，也可以重新评估这些决策。 此外，一个动作还提供了跨多个技能的共同锚点，用于定位共同指导该动作的技能区域，从而能够对这些内容进行协同修订。

sents.en: Our Work.
sents.zh: 我们的工作。

sents.en: In this work, we propose to evolve skills via trajectory-guided fault localization , which identifies the skill contents that require revision.
sents.zh: 在这项工作中，我们提出通过轨迹引导的故障定位来演化技能，该方法能够识别需要修订的技能内容。

sents.en: The key idea is that before generating any revision, we explicitly determine the edit-sites, i.e., the skill contents that should be revised, and ground this decision in behavioral evidence from execution trajectories.
sents.zh: 核心思想是：在生成任何修订之前，我们会明确确定编辑位置，即应当被修订的技能内容，并将这一决策基于执行轨迹中的行为证据。

sents.en: This idea draws on program repair, where evidence from passing and failing tests guides the localization of suspicious code before candidate patches are generated [ 38 , 36 ] .
sents.zh: 这一思路借鉴了程序修复方法，其中通过通过和失败的测试提供的证据，在生成候选补丁之前定位可疑代码 [38, 36]。

sents.en: Analogously, we treat each agent execution on a task as a test execution and the actions in its trajectory as the entities covered by that execution.
sents.zh: 类似地，我们将智能体在任务上的每次执行视为一次测试执行，并将其轨迹中的动作视为该执行所覆盖的实体。

sents.en: We localize through actions rather than treating skill contents directly as covered entities, because natural-language guidance lacks the explicit execution semantics of code.
sents.zh: 我们选择通过动作进行定位，而不是直接将技能内容视为被覆盖的实体，因为自然语言指导缺乏代码所具备的明确执行语义。

sents.en: Specifically, an agent loads a skill document as a whole, and whether and how it follows each instruction is left to its own interpretation, thus there is no observable notion of which contents an execution exercises.
sents.zh: 具体来说，智能体会将技能文档作为一个整体加载，而它是否以及如何遵循每条指令则取决于自身的解释，因此无法观察到执行究竟使用了哪些内容。

sents.en: In contrast, actions are directly observable in trajectories, differ across executions, and are shaped by the skill content.
sents.zh: 相比之下，动作在轨迹中可以直接观察，不同执行之间存在差异，并且受到技能内容的影响。

sents.en: Therefore, a deficiency in a skill manifests as suspicious actions, and the trajectory records the guidance the agent consulted when taking them, allowing these actions to be traced back to the responsible skill content.
sents.zh: 因此，技能的缺陷会表现为可疑的动作，而轨迹记录了智能体在执行这些动作时所参考的指导信息，从而可以将这些动作追溯到相应的技能内容。

sents.en: By recording these actions, the edit sites derived from them, and the evidence behind both, the localization decisions become inspectable and can be reassessed when later executions reveal a persistent problem.
sents.zh: 通过记录这些动作、由此推导出的编辑位置以及相关的证据，定位决策就变得可审查；当后续执行暴露出持续性问题时，也可以重新评估这些决策。

sents.en: An action also provides a common anchor for locating regions across multiple skills that jointly guide it, thus enabling coordinated revisions to those contents.
sents.zh: 此外，一个动作还提供了跨多个技能的共同锚点，用于定位共同指导该动作的技能区域，从而能够对这些内容进行协同修订。

paragraphs.en: We realize this idea in SkillMorph . SkillMorph first abstracts raw trajectories into sequences of state transitions, making actions and their observed effects explicit units for inspection and comparison across executions. Using these abstractions, SkillMorph localizes edit sites in two stages before generating each revision. The first stage identifies suspicious actions, i.e., those more likely to reflect deficiencies in the skills than incidental agent behaviors. Our key insight is that reliable skill evolution requires both stability, by building on effective revisions across evolution loops to avoid recurring failures, and generality, by targeting deficiencies that persist across executions and tasks. Accordingly, SkillMorph progressively aggregates behavioral evidence across executions, evolution loops, and tasks. Specifically, it first compares repeated executions of the same task and contrasts how each action occurs in failing and passing executions, where an action that introduces an error that is later recovered from in a successful execution also counts as failure evidence. It then examines how the evidence changes across evolution loops to reveal whether earlier revisions took effect, and finally aggregates the evidence across tasks to prioritize problems shared by multiple tasks. The second stage maps each suspicious action to edit sites in the skills. Our observation here is that although a trajectory does not directly reveal which instructions the agent followed, it records the skills and files consulted, narrowing the search for guidance that may have shaped an action. Based on this, an LLM-based agent uses the action’s execution context to progressively narrow the search from skills to files to specific skill content, and outputs the edit sites along with a rationale linking the skill content to the action. Finally, the edit sites, their localization rationale, and the supporting behavioral and historical evidence guide the generation of revision proposals, which are evaluated and consolidated into a patch that evolves the skill set.

paragraphs.en: Results. We evaluate SkillMorph on a repository-level software engineering skill benchmark SWE-Skills-Bench and a complex kernel-generation skill system CannBot. paragraphs.en: In this work, we focus on code agents [ 34 , 43 ] that use skills for software engineering tasks and refer to the collection of skills available to an agent as its skill set . A skill set provides procedural knowledge and project-specific context for a class of related tasks without modifying the underlying model parameters [ 19 , 42 ] . Following the Agent Skills specification [ 2 ] , each skill is a file-based package with a SKILL.md document as its entry point, as illustrated in Figure 1 . The SKILL.md ’s front matter specifies the skill’s name and description, while its body provides natural-language instructions. The package may also contain supporting resources, such as reference documents, templates, and scripts, referenced by path. Throughout this paper, skill denotes the entire package, and artifact denotes an individual file within it.

paragraphs.en: Workflow of Code Agents. In general, a code agent accesses its skill set through progressive disclosure. At startup, only the name and description of each installed skill are included in the system prompt. When a task t t arrives, the agent uses these descriptions to select relevant skills and loads their SKILL.md documents into context, and it reads supporting artifacts as needed during execution. At each step, the agent selects an action (such as reading a file, editing code, or running tests) based on the loaded instructions and accumulated context, executes it, and receives the resulting observation. This cycle continues until the task is completed or a resource limit is reached, yielding the execution trajectory
paragraphs.zh: 代码智能体的工作流程。 通常，代码智能体通过渐进式披露来访问其技能集。 启动时，系统提示中仅包含每个已安装技能的名称和描述。 当任务 t 到达时，智能体会利用这些描述选择相关技能，并将其 SKILL.md 文档加载到上下文中，在执行过程中根据需要读取支持性文件。 在每个步骤中，智能体都会根据已加载的说明和累积的上下文选择一个动作（例如读取文件、编辑代码或运行测试），执行该动作，并接收由此产生的观察结果。 这一循环将持续进行，直到任务完成或达到资源限制，从而生成执行轨迹。

paragraphs.en: As shown in the workflow, the skills affect the outcome through the actions that the agent selects under their guidance. As a result, a deficiency in the skill cannot be observed from its content alone since the agent implicitly decides whether and how to follow each instruction. Likewise, the final outcome summarizes an execution without necessarily identifying which actions caused a failure, and successful executions may include erroneous actions from which the agent later recovered. Therefore, a deficiency only manifests as problematic actions in trajectories, which tend to recur across the related tasks that the skill set serves. paragraphs.en: Equations 2 and 3 motivate three design considerations for the function Evolve \mathrm{Evolve} . First, Evolve \mathrm{Evolve} should distinguish persistent skill deficiencies from incidental agent behavior. Equation 2 defines J D J_{D} as an expectation over executions averaged across related tasks, thus a failure in one execution or task need not indicate a persistent deficiency. Moreover, Evolve \mathrm{Evolve} observes executions only on D e D_{e} , whereas its objective is evaluated on D v D_{v} . Thus, revisions that fit incidental behavior on D e D_{e} can improve J D e J_{D_{e}} without improving J D v J_{D_{v}} , motivating the identification of deficiencies that persist across executions and tasks. Second, Evolve \mathrm{Evolve} should retain and reuse historical evidence to preserve gains across evolution loops. Since 𝒮 L \mathcal{S}_{L} , rather than the most effective intermediate skill set, is returned, a revision that disrupts earlier effective guidance leaves a regression carried to 𝒮 L \mathcal{S}_{L} . Linking each revision to its motivating behavioral evidence and subsequent executions supports reassessing earlier edits and detecting these regressions. Third, Evolve \mathrm{Evolve} should support coordinated revisions across multiple skills. A task may involve several skills whose contents jointly guide the agent’s actions. Therefore, producing an improved 𝒮 i + 1 \mathcal{S}_{i+1} may require revising multiple skills, since an isolated edit can leave erroneous or conflicting guidance elsewhere. Together, these considerations motivate revising the skill contents responsible for persistent deficiencies, potentially across multiple skills, using behavioral evidence accumulated across executions, evolution loops, and tasks.

paragraphs.en: Failures under the original skill. Figure 2 ( 2(a) ) compares key execution fragments and verification results before and after evolution. In Task 1, the agent imports a document through connection A but queries through a second in-memory connection B. Since an in-memory SQLite database is private to its connection, B cannot see the imported data, and verification fails with no such table: documents (11/13 checks pass). paragraphs.en: Figure 3 illustrates the workflow of SkillMorph . Given an initial skill set 𝒮 0 \mathcal{S}_{0} and a task set D e D_{e} , SkillMorph evolves the skills over L L loops, each comprising three stages. First, Execution and Trajectory Abstraction repeatedly executes the tasks with the current skill set and abstracts the resulting trajectories into a state-transition representation, enabling comparison across executions. Using these abstractions, Suspicious Actions Localization first compares the failure and success coverage of actions across repeated executions of each task. Then, it adjusts this evidence according to changes since the preceding loop, and finally aggregates it across tasks to score and select suspicious actions. These suspicious actions guide Edit-Site Localization and Revision , which locates the relevant skills, artifacts, and contents, generates and evaluates revision proposals, and applies a patch that consolidates the selected proposals to evolve the current skill set. In addition, an evolution memory preserves execution evidence, analyses, and revision history to support these analyses. After L L loops, SkillMorph returns the resulting skill set 𝒮 L \mathcal{S}_{L} .
paragraphs.zh: 图3展示了SkillMorph的工作流程。 给定初始技能集𝒮₀ \mathcal{S}_{0}和任务集D_e D_{e}，SkillMorph会在L L个循环中演化技能，每个循环包含三个阶段。 首先，执行与轨迹抽象模块会重复使用当前技能集执行任务，并将产生的轨迹抽象为状态转移表示，从而实现不同执行过程之间的比较。 利用这些抽象结果，可疑动作定位模块首先比较每个任务在重复执行过程中各动作的失败覆盖与成功覆盖情况。 接着，该模块会根据自上一个循环以来的变化调整这些证据，并最终跨任务汇总，以评分并选出可疑动作。 这些可疑动作将指导编辑位置定位与修订模块：该模块会定位相关技能、工件和内容，生成并评估修订提案，然后应用一个整合所选提案的补丁，以演化当前的技能集。 此外，演化记忆模块会保存执行证据、分析结果和修订历史，以支持这些分析过程。 L L个循环结束后，SkillMorph将返回最终得到的技能集𝒮_L \mathcal{S}_{L}。

paragraphs.en: Task Execution To obtain a set of execution trajectories, we independently run the code agent multiple times on each evolution task under the current skill set. Repeated execution is important to SkillMorph because agent behavior is stochastic: a single run cannot separate a deficiency induced by the skills from an incidental sampling artifact [ 22 , 25 , 51 ] . Formally, in evolution loop i i , the fixed code agent 𝒜 \mathcal{A} executes each task t ∈ D e t\in D_{e} independently m m times under the current skill set 𝒮 i \mathcal{S}_{i} , producing 𝒯 i ​ ( t ) = { ( τ i , t ( j ) , y i , t ( j ) ) } j = 1 m , \mathcal{T}_{i}(t)=\{(\tau_{i,t}^{(j)},y_{i,t}^{(j)})\}_{j=1}^{m}, where τ i , t ( j ) \tau_{i,t}^{(j)} and y i , t ( j ) y_{i,t}^{(j)} denote the trajectory and final outcome of the j j -th run, respectively. Moreover, SkillMorph retains all trajectories, regardless of their outcomes, because successful and failed runs provide complementary evidence. A successful run may involve repeated unsuccessful attempts before recovery, revealing potential weaknesses in skill guidance that the final outcome alone does not expose. Conversely, a failed run may contain effective intermediate actions that remain useful despite the overall failure.

sents.en: The analysis therefore requires units that capture meaningful operations and their effects.

sents.en: Second, raw trajectories are lengthy and verbose, and similar behaviors may differ in wording, ordering, and number of steps across runs, making them difficult to compare.

paragraphs.en: This stage aims to identify the suspicious actions from the execution trajectory set 𝒯 ^ i \widehat{\mathcal{T}}_{i} that are more likely to reflect deficiencies in the current skill set 𝒮 i \mathcal{S}_{i} . The key premise is that a deficiency is a property of the skills themselves, which every execution under the skill set shares, thus the actions it induces tend to recur across independent runs and tasks. However, routine actions, such as reading files or running tests, also recur during normal execution. Therefore, recurrence alone is insufficient; we must compare how actions occur in favorable and unfavorable execution contexts. This follows the intuition of spectrum-based fault localization (SBFL), which ranks program entities by comparing their coverage in failing and passing tests, namely entities consistently covered by failing tests but seldom by passing tests warrant closer inspection [ 38 ] . We adapt this principle by treating actions as the entities to be localized and individual runs as executions. Note that FAMAS adopts a related approach to failure attribution in multi-agent systems by comparing repeated executions of the same task [ 11 ] . However, skill evolution additionally requires identifying problems shared across tasks and tracking how behavioral evidence changes as skills are revised. Therefore, we adjust each task’s spectrum counts according to their changes since the preceding loop and aggregate the adjusted evidence across tasks.

paragraphs.en: For a task t ∈ D e t\in{D}_{e} in loop i i , let 𝒯 ^ i ​ ( t ) \widehat{\mathcal{T}}_{i}(t) denote the set of its m m runs, each comprising an abstracted trajectory τ ^ \hat{\tau} and its outcome y y . We say that a run covers an action a a if its trajectory contains at least one occurrence of a a , i.e., a k = a a_{k}=a for some step k k . We then count the runs that provide failure and success coverage of a a according to the following rules. If y y indicates a failure, every action occurring in the run directly receives failure coverage, as a statement executed by a failing test does in SBFL. If y y indicates a success, we further inspect whether an action introduced an error that the agent later recovered from during the execution. This inspection is necessary because LLM-based agents typically repair their own errors, so a successful run may still contain errors that an action introduced and the agent later recovered from. However, such recovery varies across runs: the same error that is repaired in one run may remain unresolved in another, causing the run to fail. Counting every action of a successful run as success coverage would therefore exonerate the very actions that cause failures elsewhere. Moreover, even when the recovery succeeds, an action that introduces an error still reveals a deficiency, since the skill should ideally guide the agent to avoid both the error and the cost of recovering from it. We thus inspect each occurrence of an action at step k k in a successful run. Specifically, we adopt an LLM to examine the window of h h steps before and after k k , i.e., the states and actions from μ k − h − 1 \mu_{k-h-1} to μ k + h \mu_{k+h} , and thus to decide whether the action introduced an error state (an unresolved error or a failed validation) rather than merely revealing an existing one. If so, the occurrence contributes failure coverage; otherwise, it contributes success coverage. Note that this LLM-based judgment is deliberately narrow: it asks only whether the states around an action show an error that the action introduced, not which action caused a failed outcome, a question that requires reasoning over the whole trajectory and remains difficult even for strong LLMs [ 50 ] . Finally, each run contributes at most once to each coverage count of a a , so that the resulting spectrum measures how many independent executions exhibit the action rather than how often it repeats within a single run.
paragraphs.zh: 对于循环 i 中的任务 t ∈ D e t\in{D}_{e}，令 𝒯 ^ i ​ ( t ) \widehat{\mathcal{T}}_{i}(t) 表示其 m m 次运行的集合，每次运行均包含一个抽象轨迹 τ ^ \hat{\tau} 及其结果 y y。 如果某次运行的轨迹中至少出现一次动作 a a（即对于某个步骤 k k，有 a k = a a_{k}=a），我们就称该次运行覆盖了动作 a a。 随后，我们根据以下规则统计为动作 a a 提供失败覆盖和成功覆盖的运行次数。 如果 y y 表示失败，则运行中出现的每个动作都直接获得失败覆盖，这与 SBFL 中失败的测试所执行的操作一致。 如果 y y 表示成功，我们还需进一步检查某个动作是否在执行过程中引入了错误，而智能体随后又修复了该错误。 这种检查是必要的，因为基于 LLM 的智能体通常会自行修复错误，因此一次成功的运行可能仍包含由某个动作引入、但被智能体后续修复的错误。 然而，这种修复在不同运行中并不一致：同一错误在一次运行中被修复，但在另一次运行中可能仍未解决，导致该次运行失败。 因此，若将成功运行中的每个动作都计为成功覆盖，就会使那些在其他情况下引发失败的动作被错误地视为无责。 此外，即使修复成功，引入错误的动作仍然暴露了缺陷，因为理想情况下，该技能应能引导智能体同时避免错误及其修复成本。 因此，我们对成功运行中每一步骤 k k 处出现的每个动作进行单独检查。 具体而言，我们采用一个 LLM 来审查步骤 k k 前后 h h 步的窗口（即从 μ k − h − 1 \mu_{k-h-1} 到 μ k + h \mu_{k+h} 的状态与动作），从而判断该动作是否引入了错误状态（未解决的错误或验证失败），而不仅仅是揭示了既存问题。 若是如此，该次出现即贡献失败覆盖；否则，则贡献成功覆盖。 请注意，这种基于 LLM 的判断是有意限制范围的：它仅询问围绕某个动作的状态是否显示出由该动作引入的错误，而非哪个动作导致了失败结果——后者需要对整个轨迹进行推理，即便对强大的 LLM 而言仍具有挑战性 [ 50 ]。 最后，每次运行对动作 a a 的每种覆盖计数最多仅贡献一次，因此最终得到的分布谱衡量的是有多少次独立执行涉及该动作，而非它在单次运行中重复出现的次数。

paragraphs.en: Single-Task Analysis. paragraphs.en: Historical Analysis. The counts above describe how an action occurs in the current loop, but not how this evidence has evolved. The same counts can arise from a deficiency that the preceding revision has partly resolved, one that it failed to fix, or a regression that it introduced, yet these cases call for different priorities. To address this, we compare each task’s current coverage counts with those of the preceding loop and adjust them accordingly. The key insight is that, between two adjacent loops, only the skill set differs, owing to the revision made in the preceding loop. The change in coverage counts can thus be read as an effect of that revision. Specifically, we adjust failure and success coverages according to the direction of their change. For failure coverage, a decrease suggests that the revision has taken effect, so we downweight the current failure evidence to avoid repeatedly revisiting problems that may already be improving. An increase suggests that the revision was ineffective or misdirected, thus we upweight the evidence to highlight actions increasingly associated with failure. This includes newly observed actions, whose failure coverage rises from zero and may indicate a regression introduced by the revision. Success coverage serves as contrasting evidence in the suspiciousness calculation, and its change carries the reverse implication. An action whose success coverage grows may be an effective practice that the revision has promoted, thus we upweight its success evidence to shield it from suspicion, whereas a decrease weakens this contrasting evidence. When coverage remains unchanged or no comparable history is available, the adjustment is neutral, so a persistent deficiency retains its full weight while improving ones are downweighted. Together, these adjustments account for both the current evidence and its direction of change across evolution loops.

paragraphs.en: Edit-Site Localization. A skill set generally consists of natural-language instructions, together with reference documents, templates, and scripts spread over multiple skills and artifacts, which makes it hard to link an action to the contents that guide it by static rules. We address this challenge with an LLM-based agent that reads the skill set and maps each of the suspicious actions a ⋆ ∈ A ⋆ a^{\star}\in{A^{\star}} to the edit sites in the current skill set.
paragraphs.zh: 编辑位置定位。 技能集通常由自然语言指令以及分布在多个技能和工件中的参考文档、模板和脚本组成，这使得通过静态规则将某个动作与其指导内容关联起来变得困难。 我们采用一种基于大语言模型（LLM）的智能体来解决这一挑战：该智能体能读取技能集，并将每个可疑动作 a ⋆ ∈ A ⋆ a^{\star}\in{A^{\star}} 映射到当前技能集中的编辑位置。

sents.en: We address this challenge with an LLM-based agent that reads the skill set and maps each of the suspicious actions a ⋆ ∈ A ⋆ a^{\star}\in{A^{\star}} to the edit sites in the current skill set.
sents.zh: 我们采用一种基于大语言模型（LLM）的智能体来解决这一挑战：该智能体能读取技能集，并将每个可疑动作 a ⋆ ∈ A ⋆ a^{\star}\in{A^{\star}} 映射到当前技能集中的编辑位置。

paragraphs.en: For each a ⋆ a^{\star} , the agent walks through the skill set 𝒮 i \mathcal{S}_{i} recursively, narrowing from skills to artifacts to contents, rather than processing it all at once, since the latter would bring irrelevant contents (e.g., skills unrelated to a ⋆ a^{\star} ) into its context and add noise to the localization. Specifically, it first examines the occurrences of a ⋆ a^{\star} and their execution contexts in the trajectories retained during aggregation, alongside the skill descriptions and the recorded skill usage, to identify the skills that guide these actions. Then, it inspects the SKILL.md files of these skills and the artifacts they reference to find the instructions or script logic relevant to the actions. Next, it compares the prescribed actions and applicability conditions in these contents with the actions, revealing where the guidance prescribes unsuitable actions, omits necessary conditions, or conflicts with related contents, and accordingly these places are the edit sites. Finally, the agent outputs an edit-site for a ⋆ a^{\star} , together with the supporting execution evidence and a rationale that links the skill contents to the action. In particular, an edit site specifies the set of skill contents to be revised, represented by their line ranges together with the corresponding skills and artifacts. paragraphs.en: Revision Generation and Application Based on the identified edit-sites, SkillMorph next develops revision proposals and implements them as patches to evolve the skills. Specifically, we first prompt an LLM to generate a revision proposal for each edit site, specifying the intended revisions and their rationale. The proposal generation draws on three complementary sources of information. First, the edit site with its current contents and the localization rationale, which reveal what the existing skill contents prescribe and why they fail, and thus guide how to revise the site without introducing redundancy or conflicts. Second, the action a ⋆ a^{\star} associated with the edit site and its execution contexts in the trajectories, which specify the problem that the revision should address. Third, the revision history, i.e., the earlier revisions to the relevant skills together with the changes in the failure and success coverage of a ⋆ a^{\star} between adjacent loops (measured by Eq. 5 ), which show whether the earlier edits took effect, so that the new revision can retain, refine, or revert them instead of repeating ineffective changes. In addition, we explicitly specify the structure of each revision proposal, including the coordinated changes required across the involved skills or artifacts to maintain consistency.
paragraphs.zh: 基于已识别的编辑位点，SkillMorph 接下来会生成修订提案，并将其作为补丁实施，以演进技能。 具体而言，我们首先提示一个大语言模型为每个编辑位点生成修订提案，明确说明预期的修订内容及其理由。 提案的生成依赖于三个互补的信息来源。 第一是编辑位点本身及其当前内容以及局部化理由，这些揭示了现有技能内容规定了什么、为何会失败，从而指导如何修订该位点而不会引入冗余或冲突。 第二是与该编辑位点相关的动作 a ⋆ a^{\star} 及其在轨迹中的执行上下文，这些明确了修订需要解决的问题。 第三是修订历史，即对相关技能的早期修订，以及相邻循环之间 a ⋆ a^{\star} 的失败和成功覆盖范围的变化（通过公式 5 衡量），这些历史数据表明早期编辑是否生效，以便新的修订可以保留、优化或撤销这些修改，而不是重复无效的改变。 此外，我们还明确指定了每个修订提案的结构，包括在相关技能或工件之间所需的协调性变更，以保持一致性。

paragraphs.en: The proposals of different edit sites can overlap, and not all of them are worth applying (e.g., some duplicate existing skill contents). Therefore, we evaluate the proposals and select a subset for developing the final patch, instead of applying them directly. Specifically, we design a chain-of-thought prompt that guides the LLM through three steps. First, the LLM evaluates the proposals in three aspects: (1) the evidence of the proposal’s action a ⋆ a^{\star} , i.e., its suspiciousness score s i ​ ( a ⋆ ) s_{i}(a^{\star}) and the runs and tasks in which it provides failure coverage, together with the localization rationale, which indicate how strongly the problem is established, how many failures the revision can address, and how certain the localization is; (2) the proposal and the current skill contents around its edit sites, which show whether the change duplicates or conflicts with the existing guidance and whether it extends beyond what the evidence supports; and (3) the successful cases and the revision history, i.e., the successful runs that rely on the edited contents and the observed effects of earlier revisions, which show whether the change may disrupt guidance supporting successful executions or undo an effective earlier revision. Based on the evaluation, the LLM then selects the high-value proposals. Finally, it consolidates the selected proposals into the final patch, resolving any overlap among them. paragraphs.en: ∙ \bullet Skill-Evolution Approaches. We select comparison methods based on three criteria: (1) Their source code is publicly available, enabling reproduction and adaptation. (2) They demonstrate strong performance in their original evaluation settings. (3) Their skill-evolution workflows can be adapted to our benchmarks by integrating the corresponding task-execution and verification procedures. Based on these criteria, we select four representative skill-evolution approaches. SkillOpt [ 44 ] directly optimizes a single skill document through rollout-guided textual edits and validation gating. SkillAdaptor [ 46 ] first localizes an actionable fault in a failed trajectory, then revises a responsible skill or generates a new one when skill coverage is missing. EvoSkill [ 1 ] evolves complete structured skill folders through failure-driven mutations and Pareto-frontier selection based on validation performance. CAP-Evolve [ 6 ] evolves agent prompts, skill packages, and tools through an iterative workflow of failure diagnosis, candidate generation, and validation-based selection.
paragraphs.zh: ∙ \bullet 技能演化方法。 我们基于三个标准来选择比较方法：(1) 它们的源代码是公开可用的，从而可以重现和适配。 (2) 它们在原始评估设置中表现出强劲的性能。 (3) 通过将相应的任务执行和验证流程整合进来，它们的技能演化工作流程可以适配我们的基准测试。 基于这些标准，我们选择了四种具有代表性的技能演化方法。 SkillOpt [ 44 ] 通过基于展开过程的文本编辑和验证门控机制，直接优化单个技能文档。 SkillAdaptor [ 46 ] 首先定位失败轨迹中的可操作故障，然后在技能覆盖不足时修改相关技能或生成新技能。 EvoSkill [ 1 ] 通过由失败驱动的变异以及基于验证性能的帕累托前沿选择，演化完整的结构化技能文件夹。 CAP-Evolve [ 6 ] 通过一个迭代工作流程演化智能体提示、技能包和工具，该流程包括故障诊断、候选生成和基于验证的选择。

paragraphs.en: Metrics. We use three metrics to evaluate effectiveness. A trial is considered successful only if the agent completes the task within the time limit and passes all tests or verification checks provided by the benchmark. Following prior work on code generation and agent evaluation [ 8 , 45 ] , we use pass@3 and pass 3 to measure the proportions of tasks solved in at least one of three independent trials and in all three trials, respectively. In addition, we use trial-level accuracy to measure the proportion of successful individual trials.
paragraphs.zh: 指标。 我们使用三个指标来评估有效性。 仅当智能体在时限内完成任务并通过基准测试提供的所有测试或验证检查时，一次试验才被视为成功。 遵循代码生成和智能体评估领域的前期研究 [8, 45]，我们分别使用 pass@3 和 pass 3 来衡量任务在至少一次独立试验中以及在全部三次试验中均被解决的比例。 此外，我们还使用试验级准确率来衡量单次试验成功所占的比例。

paragraphs.en: Implementation. We implement SkillMorph in Python 3.11 following its three-stage workflow. We use Claude Code [ 3 ] with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 [ 9 ] as the code agent for task execution using skills, and the same model throughout evolution. To reduce wall-clock time, we parallelize task-level analyses across independent tasks. Unless otherwise stated, each evolution task is independently executed m = 3 m=3 times per loop, with L = 3 L=3 loops for SWE-Skills-Bench and L = 5 L=5 for CannBot. Task execution follows SWE-Skills-Bench’s timeout settings, while CannBot uses a 9,000-second limit. Each loop selects the top-10 suspicious actions as inputs to edit-site localization.
paragraphs.zh: 实现。 我们遵循其三阶段工作流程，使用 Python 3.11 实现了 SkillMorph。 我们使用 Claude Code [ 3 ] 和 DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 [ 9 ] 作为执行任务的代码智能体，并在整个演化过程中始终使用同一模型。 为减少实际运行时间，我们将任务级别的分析并行化到各个独立任务中。 除非另有说明，每个演化任务在每个循环中均独立执行 m = 3 m=3 次，其中 SWE-Skills-Bench 的循环次数为 L = 3 L=3，CannBot 的循环次数为 L = 5 L=5。 任务执行遵循 SWE-Skills-Bench 的超时设置，而 CannBot 则使用 9,000 秒的时限。 每个循环都会选择排名前十的可疑操作作为 edit-site 本地化的输入。

paragraphs.en: To assess generalization to tasks unseen during evolution, the tasks are divided into an evolution set D e D_{e} , which provides execution evidence for skill evolution, and a held-out evaluation set D v D_{v} , which is never accessed during evolution. For each skill in SWE-Skills-Bench, we partition its ten tasks into two five-task folds, A and B, containing tasks with odd- and even-numbered original IDs, respectively. We conduct two complementary experiments, A → \rightarrow B and B → \rightarrow A, by swapping the folds’ roles as D e D_{e} and D v D_{v} , with both experiments starting from the same original skill. Because CannBot incurs substantially higher execution costs, we use a single fixed split with 15 tasks for evolution and 15 for held-out evaluation. For each set, an LLM selects 10 Level-1 and 5 Level-2 tasks from NPUKernelBench, prioritizing task diversity.
paragraphs.zh: 为了评估模型对进化过程中未接触过的任务的泛化能力，我们将任务分为进化集 D e D_{e}（用于提供技能进化的执行证据）和保留的评估集 D v D_{v}（在进化过程中从未被访问）。 对于 SWE-Skills-Bench 中的每个技能，我们将其十个任务划分为两个各含五个任务的子集 A 和 B，分别包含原始 ID 为奇数和偶数的任务。 我们通过交换子集作为 D e D_{e} 和 D v D_{v} 的角色，开展两个互补的实验：A → \rightarrow B 和 B → \rightarrow A，且两个实验均从相同的原始技能开始。 由于 CannBot 的执行成本显著更高，我们采用单一固定划分方案：15 个任务用于进化，15 个用于保留评估。 对于每个集合，一个 LLM 会从 NPUKernelBench 中选择 10 个 Level-1 任务和 5 个 Level-2 任务，并优先确保任务的多样性。

paragraphs.en: Effectiveness. As shown in the last row of Table 1 , SkillMorph achieves 95.51% (=468/490) pass@3 and 88.37% (=433/490) pass 3 on the 490 SWE-Skills-Bench tasks. paragraphs.en: Efficiency. We examine the average time spent in an evolution loop. Each loop involves task execution by the code agent, as well as analysis and revision by the SkillMorph framework. Specifically, the latter includes trajectory abstraction, suspicious actions localization, and skill edit-site localization and revision. SkillMorph takes approximately 49 minutes per loop for a SWE-Skills-Bench skill and 127 minutes for CannBot. In particular, code-agent task execution takes 19.8 and 97.8 minutes, respectively. The three framework components take 3.1, 7.4, and 18.3 minutes on SWE-Skills-Bench, respectively, while the corresponding times on CannBot are 4.4, 5.6, and 19.0 minutes. Although code-agent execution takes nearly five times as long on CannBot as on SWE-Skills-Bench, the combined time spent on framework analysis and revision remains similar across the two benchmarks. Consequently, code-agent execution accounts for most of the difference in evolution time between the two benchmarks.
paragraphs.zh: 效率。 我们考察了演化循环中平均花费的时间。 每个循环都包括代码智能体执行任务，以及 SkillMorph 框架进行的分析与修订。 具体而言，后者包括轨迹抽象、可疑动作定位，以及技能编辑位置的定位与修订。 对于 SWE-Skills-Bench 中的技能，SkillMorph 每个循环大约需要 49 分钟；而对于 CannBot，则需要 127 分钟。 其中，代码智能体执行任务分别耗时 19.8 分钟和 97.8 分钟。 在 SWE-Skills-Bench 中，框架的三个组件分别耗时 3.1、7.4 和 18.3 分钟；而在 CannBot 上，对应的时间分别为 4.4、5.6 和 19.0 分钟。 尽管代码智能体在 CannBot 上的执行时间几乎是 SWE-Skills-Bench 的五倍，但框架分析与修订的总耗时在这两个基准测试中仍然相近。 因此，代码智能体的执行时间构成了这两个基准测试之间演化时间差异的主要部分。

paragraphs.en: Generalizability. SkillMorph remains effective not only across different task splits within SWE-Skills-Bench but also across skill systems that differ in structure, scale, and task domain. Under the two complementary task splits described in Section 5.1 , A → \rightarrow B achieves 97.55% (=239/245) pass@3, 95.24% (=700/735) trial-level accuracy, and 92.65% (=227/245) pass 3 , while B → \rightarrow A achieves 93.47% (=229/245), 89.25% (=656/735), and 84.08% (=206/245), respectively. Although performance differs between the two split directions, both achieve high held-out scores across all three metrics, indicating that the evolved skills generalize to tasks unseen during evolution. SWE-Skills-Bench evaluates compact, independent skills for repository-level software engineering, whereas CannBot involves larger, coordinated skills for AscendC kernel generation. paragraphs.en: Against existing methods on SWE-Skills-Bench, SkillMorph solves 16 more tasks than CAP-Evolve, the strongest baseline, and 48 more than EvoSkill, corresponding to pass@3 gains of 3.27 and 9.80 percentage points. More notably, the gain is larger for consistently solved tasks in every baseline comparison, ranging from 17 to 68 tasks (3.47–13.88 points in pass 3 ). Consistent with these gains, SkillMorph records 42–174 additional successful trials out of 1,470, raising trial-level accuracy by 2.86–11.84 percentage points. The advantage in execution consistency is particularly clear on CannBot. Although CAP-Evolve matches SkillMorph in pass@3 (14/15), SkillMorph solves all 14 tasks in every trial, compared with 8–11 among the four baselines, giving a pass 3 advantage of 20.00–40.00 percentage points. This greater consistency is also reflected at the trial level, where SkillMorph records 4–10 additional successes out of 45 trials and raises accuracy by 8.89–22.22 percentage points. These results indicate that SkillMorph ’s advantage extends from covering additional tasks to supporting more consistent success across repeated executions.
paragraphs.zh: 在与 SWE-Skills-Bench 上现有方法的对比中，SkillMorph 比最强的基线模型 CAP-Evolve 多解决了 16 个任务，比 EvoSkill 多解决了 48 个任务，对应的 pass@3 提升幅度分别为 3.27 和 9.80 个百分点。 更值得注意的是，在所有基线模型的对比中，持续成功解决的任务数量带来的提升更大，范围从 17 到 68 个任务（pass@3 提升 3.47–13.88 个百分点）。 与这些提升一致，SkillMorph 在 1,470 次试验中记录了 42–174 次额外的成功尝试，使试验级别的准确率提升了 2.86–11.84 个百分点。 在执行一致性方面的优势在 CannBot 上表现得尤为明显。 尽管 CAP-Evolve 在 pass@3（14/15）上与 SkillMorph 表现一致，但 SkillMorph 在每次试验中都成功解决了全部 14 个任务，而四个基线模型中仅有 8–11 个任务被解决，这使得 pass@3 的优势达到了 20.00–40.00 个百分点。 这种更高的一致性也体现在试验层面：SkillMorph 在 45 次试验中记录了 4–10 次额外的成功，并将准确率提升了 8.89–22.22 个百分点。 这些结果表明，SkillMorph 的优势不仅体现在覆盖更多任务上，还体现在重复执行过程中能够更稳定地取得成功。

paragraphs.en: Fine-Grained Comparison. We further compare improvements and regressions at the task and skill levels relative to the original skills to understand how the overall gains are distributed. At the task level, we classify a task as improved, unchanged, or regressed according to whether its number of successful trials out of three increases, remains the same, or decreases. At the skill level, we use the same categories, comparing pass@3 first and using trial-level accuracy to break ties. Figure 4 presents task-level changes on both benchmarks and skill-level changes on SWE-Skills-Bench.

paragraphs.en: On SWE-Skills-Bench, SkillMorph improves a similar number of tasks to CAP-Evolve (126 versus 122), but introduces substantially fewer regressions (9 versus 36). paragraphs.en: In this section, we evaluate how the number of evolution loops affects SkillMorph ’s effectiveness and conduct an ablation study to assess the contributions of its key components.
paragraphs.zh: 在本节中，我们将评估进化循环的数量如何影响 SkillMorph 的有效性，并进行消融研究以评估其关键组件的贡献。

paragraphs.en: Effect of Evolution Loops. We examine the original skills and skills produced after each of the three SWE-Skills-Bench loops and five CannBot loops. Each version is evaluated on the same held-out tasks under the protocol described in Section 5.1 . As shown in Figure 5 , the first loop produces large gains in all three metrics on both benchmarks. Although some scores decline in intermediate loops, all three metrics reach their highest values in the final loop. On SWE-Skills-Bench, the first loop raises pass 3 from 67.96% to 85.31% and accounts for 85–88% of the final gain across the three metrics. From the first to the third loop, pass 3 increases by 3.06 percentage points, compared with 1.63 points for pass@3, despite a decline in the second loop. On CannBot, the first loop increases pass@3 from 12 to 13 of 15 tasks and pass 3 from 7 to 9. Pass@3 reaches 14 tasks by the second loop and remains there, whereas pass 3 falls from 12 to 11 in the intermediate loops before reaching 14 in the fifth. Together, these results show that early loops produce most of the gains in task coverage, while later loops can improve execution consistency despite intermediate declines.

paragraphs.en: Effect of Components. We conduct an ablation study to assess the contributions of repeated execution, the use of history, and skill edit-site localization. We construct three variants of SkillMorph : Single-run executes each evolution task once per loop ( m = 1 m=1 ) while retaining the same number of loops; w/o History omits the historical adjustment of action coverage counts and excludes historical information from proposal generation and evaluation; and w/o Localization skips Skill Edit-Site Localization and generates revisions directly from the selected suspicious actions and their execution contexts. Table 2 reports the performance of SkillMorph variants with different component configurations on both benchmarks, measured by pass@3, trial-level accuracy, and pass 3 . Single-run has the largest effect on pass@3, lowering it by 5.31 (=26/490) and 13.33 (=2/15) percentage points on SWE-Skills-Bench and CannBot, respectively. Removing localization has the largest effect on pass 3 , lowering it by 6.12 (=30/490) and 33.33 (=5/15) points, respectively. The w/o History variant has the smallest effect on both benchmarks, with CannBot pass@3 unchanged but lower trial-level accuracy and pass 3 . These results suggest that repeated execution contributes most clearly to task coverage, while explicit localization is particularly important for consistent success.

paragraphs.en: We apply SkillMorph in collaboration with a team that develops AI operators to evolve the skills used in automated kernel generation. The evaluation covers 63 AI operators of varying complexity, with test cases spanning multiple data types and tensor shapes. Execution evidence from these tasks guides skill revisions addressing numerical correctness, kernel performance, and the AI operators’ development and verification workflow. We have submitted these skill revisions in 6 pull requests, all of which have been accepted by the developers. The collaboration is ongoing, and the team continues to use and refine the revised skills.

paragraphs.en: ∙ \bullet Skill Authoring. We observe that instructions to test thoroughly can still leave verification blocked after the requested code changes are completed. In these cases, the skill lacks concrete guidance on dependency handling, verification environments, or re-verification after repairs. This suggests that skill authors should specify the applicability conditions, required execution order, and completion criteria of key operations, using actual trajectories to identify gaps in the guidance. This observation aligns with prior work emphasizing procedural guidance and verification feedback [ 14 ] . When such guidance spans multiple files, the main instructions should clearly reference the relevant materials, and related rules should remain consistent across documents and scripts.
paragraphs.zh: ∙ \bullet 技能编写。 我们观察到，即使按照要求完成代码更改，彻底测试的指令仍可能导致验证受阻。 在这些情况下，该技能缺乏关于依赖项处理、验证环境或修复后重新验证的具体指导。 这表明，技能编写者应明确关键操作的适用条件、所需执行顺序和完成标准，并利用实际轨迹识别指导中的不足。 这一观察结果与强调流程指导和验证反馈的先前研究一致 [ 14 ] 。 当此类指导涉及多个文件时，主指令应明确引用相关材料，且相关规则应在不同文档和脚本中保持一致。

paragraphs.en: ∙ \bullet Task-Specific Adaptation. Experience accumulated through cross-task evolution may still leave difficulties specific to the current task unresolved. In our bidirectional cross-validation, 21 tasks failed in all three evaluation runs with both the original skill and the skill evolved using the opposite task fold. We examined the evolution records in which these tasks themselves belonged to the task set used for evolution. Relative to their initial executions in those records, five tasks subsequently succeeded in at least one run, while four others showed improvements in individual verification checks. These observations suggest that task-specific feedback may complement experience accumulated across tasks. Reflexion [ 30 ] uses feedback-driven reflection to guide subsequent attempts, while Voyager [ 32 ] stores verified programs for reuse. Building on these mechanisms, future work could explore combining task-level adaptation with SkillMorph to address immediate blockers and turn verified recovery operations and their applicability conditions into reusable skill guidance.

paragraphs.en: Threats to Validity The main threat to internal validity arises from stochastic execution and the adaptation of the compared approaches. To reduce this threat, we use their official implementations under the common experimental protocol described in Section 5.1 and evaluate each task in three independent trials. The main threat to external validity lies in the selection of skill systems and tasks. To mitigate this threat, we evaluate SkillMorph on held-out tasks from SWE-Skills-Bench and CannBot, which differ in task domain and skill structure. We also swap the tasks used for evolution and evaluation on SWE-Skills-Bench to reduce dependence on a particular task split. The main threat to construct validity lies in the metrics used to assess skill quality. To reduce this threat, we use pass@3, trial-level accuracy, and pass 3 to provide complementary measures of task completion and consistency across repeated executions.
paragraphs.zh: 效度威胁 对内部效度的主要威胁源于随机执行以及所比较方法的适应性变化。 为降低这一威胁，我们在第 5.1 节描述的通用实验协议下使用其官方实现，并对每个任务进行三次独立试验评估。 对外部效度的主要威胁在于技能系统和任务的选择。 为缓解这一威胁，我们在 SWE-Skills-Bench 和 CannBot 中预留的任务上评估 SkillMorph，这些任务在任务域和技能结构上有所不同。 我们还交换了 SWE-Skills-Bench 上用于进化和评估的任务，以减少对特定任务划分的依赖。 对构念效度的主要威胁在于用于评估技能质量的指标。 为降低这一威胁，我们使用 pass@3、试验级准确率和 pass 3，以提供任务完成度和重复执行中一致性的互补性衡量标准。

paragraphs.en: Agent Skill Construction and Evolution. Agent skills package reusable procedural knowledge, while their utility depends on the compatibility among the skill, task, and execution context [ 19 , 12 ] . Existing methods for improving agent skills can be broadly divided into skill construction and skill evolution. Skill construction derives new artifacts from execution experience, such as executable libraries, consolidated trajectory lessons, or skills authored by a meta-skill [ 32 , 26 , 48 ] . Skill evolution instead revises existing artifacts from execution feedback, either through optimization loops based on failure analysis, generated evaluation tasks, or validation-gated edits [ 1 , 31 , 44 ] , or by diagnosing defects from trajectories [ 23 , 46 , 33 ] . SkillMorph links suspicious-action analysis across tasks and evolution loops to explicit edit-site localization and coordinated skill revisions.
paragraphs.zh: 智能体技能构建与演化。 智能体技能包封装了可重复使用的前置知识，但其效用取决于技能、任务与执行上下文之间的兼容性 [ 19 , 12 ] 。 现有提升智能体技能的方法大致可分为技能构建和技能演化两类。 技能构建通过执行经验生成新的成果，例如可执行的库、整合后的轨迹经验，或由元技能编写的技能 [ 32 , 26 , 48 ] 。 技能演化则基于执行反馈修改现有成果，方式包括依据失败分析进行优化循环、利用生成的评估任务或验证受限的编辑操作 [ 1 , 31 , 44 ] ，亦或通过诊断轨迹中的缺陷实现 [ 23 , 46 , 33 ] 。 SkillMorph 将跨任务和演化循环的可疑动作分析与明确的编辑位置定位及协同的技能修订相连接。

paragraphs.en: Agent Trajectory Analysis and Utilization. Beyond skill evolution, agent execution trajectories have also been widely studied for behavior analysis [ 5 , 29 ] , failure diagnosis [ 7 , 50 , 11 ] , and context management [ 21 , 28 , 39 ] . For example, Bouzenia and Pradel [ 5 ] characterize the behavioral differences between successful and unsuccessful executions of software engineering agents. FAMAS [ 11 ] adapts spectrum-based fault localization to multi-agent systems, contrasting successful and failed executions to attribute failures to the responsible agent actions. AgentDiet [ 39 ] removes redundant and expired information to reduce coding-agent inference cost. Unlike these works, which analyze or manage trajectories without revising persistent artifacts, SkillMorph links behavioral evidence to editable skill artifacts and tracks their revisions across evolution loops.
paragraphs.zh: 智能体轨迹分析与利用。 除了技能演化之外，智能体的执行轨迹也被广泛用于行为分析 [5, 29]、故障诊断 [7, 50, 11] 和上下文管理 [21, 28, 39]。 例如，Bouzenia 和 Pradel [5] 描述了软件工程智能体在执行成功与失败时的行为差异。 FAMAS [11] 将基于谱的故障定位方法应用于多智能体系统，通过对比成功与失败的执行过程，将故障归因于相应的智能体动作。 AgentDiet [39] 会移除冗余和过期的信息，以降低编码智能体的推理成本。 与这些研究不同，它们虽然分析或管理轨迹，但并未修改持久化产物；而 SkillMorph 则将行为证据与可编辑的技能产物关联起来，并追踪其在演化循环中的修订过程。

paragraphs.en: Feedback-Driven Software Improvement. Using execution feedback to improve software has a long history [ 16 , 13 , 38 ] , among which automated program repair (APR) is a representative line of research [ 36 , 37 , 41 , 40 ] . APR leverages tests throughout the repair loop: fault localization contrasts passing and failing executions to rank suspicious program entities [ 38 ] , and candidate patches are searched for and validated against test results, as exemplified by GenProg [ 36 ] . Treating the skills as evolvable software, SkillMorph follows this localize-then-revise paradigm, using spectrum-guided execution feedback to localize and revise deficient skill artifacts across evolution loops.
paragraphs.zh: 基于反馈的软件改进。 利用执行反馈来改进软件已有悠久的历史 [ 16 , 13 , 38 ]，其中自动化程序修复（APR）是一项具有代表性的研究方向 [ 36 , 37 , 41 , 40 ]。 APR 在整个修复循环中利用测试：故障定位通过对比通过和失败的执行来对可疑的程序实体进行排序 [ 38]，而候选补丁则通过搜索并依据测试结果进行验证，GenProg 就是其中的典型示例 [ 36]。 SkillMorph 将技能视为可演化的软件，遵循“先定位后修订”的范式，利用谱引导的执行反馈，在演化循环中定位并修订有缺陷的技能产物。

sents.en: Using execution feedback to improve software has a long history [ 16 , 13 , 38 ] , among which automated program repair (APR) is a representative line of research [ 36 , 37 , 41 , 40 ] .
sents.zh: 利用执行反馈来改进软件已有悠久的历史 [ 16 , 13 , 38 ]，其中自动化程序修复（APR）是一项具有代表性的研究方向 [ 36 , 37 , 41 , 40 ]。

sents.en: APR leverages tests throughout the repair loop: fault localization contrasts passing and failing executions to rank suspicious program entities [ 38 ] , and candidate patches are searched for and validated against test results, as exemplified by GenProg [ 36 ] .
sents.zh: APR 在整个修复循环中利用测试：故障定位通过对比通过和失败的执行来对可疑的程序实体进行排序 [ 38]，而候选补丁则通过搜索并依据测试结果进行验证，GenProg 就是其中的典型示例 [ 36]。

sents.en: Treating the skills as evolvable software, SkillMorph follows this localize-then-revise paradigm, using spectrum-guided execution feedback to localize and revise deficient skill artifacts across evolution loops.
sents.zh: SkillMorph 将技能视为可演化的软件，遵循“先定位后修订”的范式，利用谱引导的执行反馈，在演化循环中定位并修订有缺陷的技能产物。

paragraphs.en: In this paper, we propose SkillMorph , a skill-evolution approach for LLM-based agents based on trajectory-guided edit-site localization. SkillMorph explicitly determines the edit sites, i.e., the skill contents that should be revised, before generating any revision, and grounds this decision in behavioral evidence from execution trajectories. In particular, SkillMorph abstracts raw trajectories into sequences of state transitions, progressively aggregates evidence across repeated executions, evolution loops, and tasks to identify suspicious actions, and then traces each suspicious action back to edit sites that may span multiple skills, together with a rationale linking the skill content to the action. Experimental results on SWE-Skills-Bench and CannBot demonstrate the effectiveness of SkillMorph . Compared with the original skills, SkillMorph achieves relative improvements of 15.84% in pass@3 and 30.03% in pass 3 on SWE-Skills-Bench, and 16.67% and 100% on CannBot, respectively, consistently outperforming the improvements achieved by all the four compared approaches. Moreover, in a deployment with our collaboration partner, SkillMorph produced six skill-revision pull requests that have been accepted for future AI operator development, further showing its practical value.
paragraphs.zh: 在本文中，我们提出了 SkillMorph——一种基于轨迹引导的编辑位定位方法，用于实现 LLM 智能体的技能演化。 SkillMorph 在生成任何修订内容之前，会明确确定编辑位，即需要修改的技能内容，并将这一决策建立在执行轨迹中的行为证据之上。 具体而言，SkillMorph 将原始轨迹抽象为状态转换序列，通过重复执行、演化循环和任务逐步聚合证据以识别可疑操作，随后追溯每个可疑操作至可能跨越多个技能的编辑位，并附上将技能内容与操作关联起来的理由。 在 SWE-Skills-Bench 和 CannBot 上的实验结果证明了 SkillMorph 的有效性。 与原始技能相比，SkillMorph 在 SWE-Skills-Bench 上 pass@3 的相对提升为 15.84%，pass 3 的提升为 30.03%；在 CannBot 上则分别提升了 16.67% 和 100%，始终优于所有四个对比方法所取得的改进。 此外，在与我们的合作伙伴共同部署中，SkillMorph 生成了六个技能修订的拉取请求，这些请求已被接受用于未来的 AI 操作员开发，进一步证明了其实用价值。
